title: The Geopolitics of Food and Agriculture
abstract: Food has long served as an instrument of statecraft. Yet agricultural economics typically analyzes policy through the lens of consumer and producer welfare, which neglects security externalities. We review the literature at the intersection of agricultural economics and political science, examining how food systems both shape and are shaped by geopolitical forces through the two channels of ( a ) domestic instability with international spillovers and ( b ) the deliberate use of food in statecraft. Our synthesis of key findings in the literature suggests that ( a ) food prices relate to riots and instability while ambiguously relating to civil war and violence, ( b ) the wide geographic spread of agriculture limits but does not eliminate unilateral coercive leverage compared with other strategic sectors, and ( c ) domestic food policies are strongly related to national security goals. Moreover, we point out the many extant data sets one can use to do work in this area and identify several research gaps in the literature. As global uncertainty intensifies, integrating geopolitical analysis into agricultural economics is essential for policy relevance.

title: “A state university in name only”: privatization and corporatization in contemporary Sri Lankan state universities
abstract: Purpose This article examines changes in Sri Lankan state universities (i.e. public universities) in the last 3 decades through two core concepts of management: privatization and corporatization. Design/methodology/approach This article is a qualitative study using discourse analysis, focusing on practices of privatization and corporatization. I examine documentation produced by 16 state universities from 2016 to 2020 and a reflexive journal written by myself over the past 10 years. Findings The article describes the similarities in the characteristics of these two phenomena and distinguishes conceptual differences and their consequences in the Sri Lankan academic context. Sri Lankan universities show characteristics of both privatization and corporatization, which appear as practices (as described in activities) and discourses (e.g. competitiveness, unemployability). These include changes to academic work norms and corporate-like governing practices. Research limitations/implications This is an initial exploration using mostly documentary sources. Local specificities of global phenomena such as corporatization and privatization need in-depth study and the education sector is a rich setting for further research. Practical implications This has direct implications for how universities are managed in future. Social implications This article analyses the changes that come about when a public good, such as education, is privatized and corporatized insidiously. Originality/value This article contributes to the field of education and management by considering how the two phenomena, corporatization and privatization, manifest in Sri Lankan state universities, illustrating through this the local manifestations of global phenomena affecting higher education.

Transformación digital y reconfiguración institucional en el Poder Judicial peruano: tensiones, avances y límites del Expediente Judicial Electrónico
abstract: La transformación digital del sistema judicial peruano, lejos de limitarse a la incorporación de herramientas tecnológicas, configura un proceso de reconfiguración institucional cuya complejidad se manifiesta en la tensión constante entre innovación normativa, dinámicas organizacionales heredadas y condicionamientos sociopolíticos específicos. A través del estudio del Expediente Judicial Electrónico (EJE), se examinan críticamente las trayectorias de implementación tecnológica y los marcos institucionales que interactúan con las políticas de digitalización, identificando patrones de fragmentación estructural que desafían los supuestos de eficiencia y modernización frecuentemente asociados a estos procesos. Los hallazgos apuntan a una digitalización paradójica, donde la proliferación de iniciativas aisladas, la desarticulación entre actores institucionales, las debilidades en ciberseguridad y la persistencia de marcos normativos precarios configuran un escenario de vulnerabilidad estructural. En este contexto, se observa cómo las tensiones entre diseño formal y prácticas cotidianas reflejan no solo resistencias organizacionales, sino también una fragilidad de la arquitectura institucional que sostiene el proceso. Lejos de constituir una narrativa de éxito lineal, la experiencia peruana revela una modernización fragmentada en el que los avances técnicos coexisten con déficits de legitimidad, sostenibilidad y equidad, poniendo de relieve la necesidad de un enfoque sistémico que trascienda lo meramente instrumental e integre dimensiones de gobernanza, justicia social y resiliencia institucional.

title: Tindak Pidana Perdagangan Orang Sebagai Kejahatan Transnasional Dalam Perspektif Hukum Dan Hak Asasi
abstract: Trafficking in persons is a serious form of crime that has developed into a transnational crime with far-reaching implications for the protection of human rights. This crime not only constitutes a violation of national criminal law but also undermines human dignity by treating individuals as objects of economic and social exploitation. This article aims to analyze trafficking in persons as a transnational crime from the perspectives of Indonesian law and human rights, while also identifying challenges in the implementation of victim protection. This study employs normative legal research using a statutory approach and a conceptual approach. The legal materials consist of primary, secondary, and tertiary legal sources, which are analyzed qualitatively using a descriptive-analytical method. The findings indicate that Indonesia has established a relatively comprehensive legal framework through Law Number 21 of 2007 on the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, as well as through the ratification of various international legal instruments, including the Palermo Protocol. However, a gap remains between legal norms and their implementation, particularly in the areas of prevention, law enforcement, inter-agency coordination, and the fulfillment of victims' rights. Victims of trafficking continue to face various obstacles in obtaining restitution, rehabilitation, and sustainable social reintegration. Therefore, combating trafficking in persons requires a comprehensive approach that integrates effective law enforcement, appropriate preventive policies, and human rights-based victim protection. Such an approach is expected to strengthen the protection of human dignity while enhancing the effectiveness of efforts to combat trafficking in persons as a transnational crime. Abstrak Tindak pidana perdagangan orang merupakan salah satu bentuk kejahatan serius yang berkembang menjadi kejahatan transnasional dengan dampak luas terhadap perlindungan hak asasi manusia. Kejahatan ini tidak hanya melibatkan pelanggaran terhadap hukum pidana nasional, tetapi juga mencederai martabat manusia karena menempatkan individu sebagai objek eksploitasi ekonomi dan sosial. Artikel ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis tindak pidana perdagangan orang sebagai kejahatan transnasional dalam perspektif hukum Indonesia dan hak asasi manusia, serta mengidentifikasi tantangan dalam implementasi perlindungan terhadap korban. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode penelitian hukum normatif dengan pendekatan perundang-undangan dan pendekatan konseptual. Bahan hukum yang digunakan berupa bahan hukum primer, sekunder, dan tersier yang dianalisis secara kualitatif dengan metode deskriptif-analitis. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Indonesia telah memiliki kerangka hukum yang relatif komprehensif melalui Undang-Undang Nomor 21 Tahun 2007 tentang Pemberantasan Tindak Pidana Perdagangan Orang serta ratifikasi berbagai instrumen hukum internasional, termasuk Protokol Palermo. Namun, masih terdapat kesenjangan antara norma hukum dan implementasinya di lapangan, terutama dalam aspek pencegahan, penegakan hukum, koordinasi antarlembaga, serta pemenuhan hak-hak korban. Korban perdagangan orang masih menghadapi berbagai hambatan dalam memperoleh restitusi, rehabilitasi, dan reintegrasi sosial secara berkelanjutan. Oleh karena itu, penanggulangan tindak pidana perdagangan orang memerlukan pendekatan yang komprehensif dengan mengintegrasikan penegakan hukum yang efektif, kebijakan pencegahan yang tepat, serta perlindungan korban berbasis hak asasi manusia. Pendekatan tersebut diharapkan dapat memperkuat perlindungan terhadap martabat manusia sekaligus meningkatkan efektivitas penanggulangan perdagangan orang sebagai kejahatan transnasional.

The dimensions and realization mechanism of brand Jing-Jie(境界) initiated by brand ritual behaviours: a grounded analysis inspired by Chinese Zen Jing-Jie(境界) theory
abstract: Purpose This research seeks to explain the phenomenon of consumers' internal growth initiated by brand ritual behaviours, by establishing a novel construct “brand Jing-Jie(境界)”, inspired by Chinese Zen Jing-Jie(境界)theory. The connotation of “brand Jing-Jie(境界)” is a supplement and expansion of traditional brand loyalty. Design/methodology/approach The data collection is from 32 in-depth interviews. A grounded theory research was adopted for analysis. Findings Through exploring the realization mechanism by which brand ritual behaviours achieve brand Jing-Jie(境界), this paper explores the phenomenon of brand Jing-Jie(境界) and its three dimensions (oneness state, Zen Satori and self-realization). Specifically, brand ritual behaviours (metaphoricity, repeatability and emotionality) facilitate consumers to comprehend brand tacit knowledge (body learning, brand metaphor internalization and brand ritual meaning), thereby facilitating consumer meaning-making (meaning-confirmation, meaning-projection, meaning-expansion and meaning-negotiation), and ultimately achieving brand Jing-Jie(境界). Originality/value The findings propose a novel construct – brand Jing-Jie(境界), which achieves spiritual loyalty, transcends traditional brand loyalty and develops the consumer–brand relationship into a co-cultivation(共修) relationship. Meanwhile, it explores brand tacit knowledge that plays an important antecedent role in transforming brand knowledge into consumer wisdom; it supplements the part of brand knowledge that cannot be conveyed through language and text.

title: How entrepreneurs can bounce back after failure
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to review the latest management developments across the globe and pinpoint practical implications from cutting-edge research and case studies. Design/methodology/approach This briefing is prepared by an independent writer who adds their own impartial comments and places the articles in context. Findings Entrepreneurs looking to bounce back from failure are better positioned to succeed with new ventures if they have accrued sufficient social capital. This can enable them to build strong networks that provide exposure to new ideas, learning and potential opportunities. The emotional support such relationships generate is equally crucial, as it helps to minimize the negative effects of failure and boost confidence and entrepreneurial self-efficacy. Originality/value The briefing saves busy executives, strategists and researchers hours of reading time by selecting only the very best, most pertinent information and presenting it in a condensed and easy-to-digest format.
